posts.text:
Assange just posted “I’m back” on X.

Throwback to January 13, 2018.

Assange tweeted a chess position with no caption. It was move 24 from the 1918 Capablanca vs. Marshall game,  one of the most famous defensive games in chess history. Marshall had spent years preparing a surprise attack. Capablanca refuted it and won.

That same period, Q dropped the WarGames line “How about a nice game of chess?” followed by “FOX THREE. SPLASH.”

Anons immediately mapped it: FOX THREE = Qf3. Queen to f3 was the exact next move after the position Assange posted.

A few drops earlier, during the Atlanta airport power outage, someone asked if they had relocated a pawn or a bigger piece. Q answered with one word: BISHOP.

Atlanta went dark. Black bishop had just moved in the game Assange posted.

The theory that circulated on 8chan and the old research boards was that Assange and Q were playing the same game in public — one posting the board, the other answering with the next move in coded language.

Whether it was coordination, coincidence, or just anons connecting dots, it remains one of the coolest intersections from that era.
